The ministry's own document, dated June 2022 and hosted on its official site, sets out the Agenda National de Transformation Numérique 2022-2025 as a four-year strategy with a calendar of projects from 2022 to 2025.

The agenda is broken into 25 initiatives and 77 projects for a global investment of 400 million dollars, with a project sheet giving cost, funding mode and owner for each project (e.g. 200k EUR and 3,000k EUR for the AN-ETAT agency).

The agenda states that the State 's'est doté d'un Haut Conseil du Numérique (HCN) qui permettra de suivre l'exécution de l'Agenda', and that the HCN's Technical Support Committee should be the body responsible for monitoring and evaluating the agenda.

The agenda says several funding sources are identified for the plan, with significant support needed from development partners and the State and an active private-sector contribution (353 million euros shown in a chart); its project sheets give funding modes such as 'PTF, Etat', and it states no budget line or allocation.

The agenda's annex lists a Stratégie Nationale de Modernisation de l'Administration et des TICs 2012-2016 among the documents it draws on; the document gives no description of that strategy's scope, and its period had ended by June 2022.
